children: Amazon, the commerce and cloud-computing giant

, traded at $248.96, down 0.57%, at 10:00 a.m. ET ahead of Thursday's earnings report. The modest decline leaves the bigger question untouched: how much profit can Amazon squeeze from its AI infrastructure spending? Reuters' earnings preview frames the coming reports as a test of whether that investment can deliver durable returns.

The hurdle is already high. Amazon reported second-quarter AWS revenue growth of 37%, its fastest pace in 18 quarters, alongside $16.6 billion in cloud operating income. Companywide operating income climbed 43% to $27.5 billion. Management's third-quarter operating-income forecast of $22.5 billion to $26.5 billion puts the next report's profitability firmly in focus.

The GuruFocus snapshot shows a GF Score of 93/100, with growth its strongest category and financial strength comparatively weaker. That supports a strong operating profile, but it does not settle the spending question. Watch AWS margins, capital expenditures and capacity constraints together. Faster cloud growth carries more weight when the returns hold up after power, depreciation and chip costs.

title: Amazon Stocks Edge Lower Ahead of Earnings After 37% AWS Revenue Growth
